record.paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
record.original_question: If one succeeds, even partially, in proving global existence for the Jeffreys-type evolutionary problem, can one then construct attractors, at least generalized ones, and/or inertial manifolds for that system?

evidence.quote: В случае успешного (даже частичного) решения задачи о существовании глобальных решений встает вопрос о построении любых, пусть обобщенных, аттракторов и/или инерционных многообразий (о последнем понятии см. [70]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys type, occupying a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary, and governed by the system
$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t}+(v\cdot\nabla)v=\operatorname{Div}\sigma-\nabla p+f,\qquad \operatorname{div} v=0,\qquad v|_{\partial\Omega}=0,\qquad v|_{t=0}=v_0,$$
where the deviatoric stress tensor $\sigma$ obeys a Jeffreys-type constitutive relation
$$\sigma+\lambda_1\,\frac{\mathcal{D}\sigma}{\mathcal{D}t}=2\eta\Bigl(\mathcal{E}(v)+\lambda_2\,\frac{\mathcal{D}\mathcal{E}(v)}{\mathcal{D}t}\Bigr),$$
with $\mathcal{E}(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v+\nabla v^\top)$, relaxation time $\lambda_1>0$, retardation time $\lambda_2\in(0,\lambda_1)$, viscosity $\eta>0$, and $\mathcal{D}/\mathcal{D}t$ an objective (e.g. upper-convected, lower-convected, or Jaumann) time derivative.

Suppose that, for a given choice of objective derivative and on a given class of initial data and external forces $f$, one has established (possibly only partial) global-in-time existence of weak solutions to this system.

Problem. Under such global existence, construct dynamical objects describing the long-time behaviour of the system: namely, prove the existence of a global attractor — or, failing that, of a generalized attractor (e.g. a trajectory attractor, or an attractor in the sense of multivalued semiflows / semigroups acting on a set of admissible trajectories) — for the resulting (possibly multivalued) dynamical system associated with the weak solutions. Moreover, determine whether the system admits a finite-dimensional inertial manifold, i.e. a finite-dimensional, Lipschitz, positively invariant manifold in the phase space that contains the global attractor and attracts all trajectories at a uniform exponential rate.
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of (trajectory and global) attractors for weak solutions of the autonomous Jeffreys-type viscoelastic motion equations has been established, and non-autonomous versions with memory have been treated as well. The inertial-manifold part of the question appears not to have been resolved for the Jeffreys system: standard results require a spectral gap condition that has not been verified in this setting, so to current knowledge no inertial manifold has been constructed. Hence the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Trajectory and Global Attractors of the Boundary Value Problem for Autonomous Motion Equations of Viscoelastic Medium
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of minimal trajectory and global attractors for weak solutions of the autonomous Jeffreys-type viscoelastic motion equations.
status_evidence.claim: Global/trajectory attractors are constructed for the autonomous Jeffreys viscoelastic model, partially answering the attractor part.

status_evidence.title: Attractors for Model of Viscoelastic Media with Memory Motion in Non-Autonomous Case
status_evidence.snippet: Attractors are constructed for non-autonomous viscoelastic media with memory.
status_evidence.claim: Generalized attractors are available also in the non-autonomous regime.

status_evidence.title: Inertial manifold — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of inertial manifolds usually requires a restrictive spectral gap condition.
status_evidence.claim: No construction of an inertial manifold for the Jeffreys system is reported; the spectral gap condition is generally not verified for such fluid models.
